{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABYf5t5A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhCEPOg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 17, "title": "Add opt-in interactive DOM Overlay preview for Android AR and Quest MR", "body": "## Problem

The emulator currently declines `dom-overlay` in every mode even though developers mainly need to **see their application's existing HTML UI, interact with it, and observe the normal JavaScript events and app behavior** while testing WebXR. Prior [Issue #13](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/13) / [PR #14](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/14) and [Issue #15](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/15) / [PR #16](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/16) pursued much broader standards-level presentation, stereo DOM rendering, `beforexrselect`, shadow-tree and iframe guarantees. This proved difficult in a desktop browser extension; both Issues are administratively closed despite unfinished mandatory scope.

**Product direction change:** For now, prefer a practical, explicitly limited **Interactive DOM Overlay Preview** over complete WebXR DOM Overlay conformance. It can be enhanced later. Avoid repeating the previous impossible-to-complete conformance acceptance criteria in this Issue.

## Expected outcome

Provide an **explicitly opt-in, clearly labeled emulator-only DOM Overlay Preview** that can show the application's **original live `domOverlay.root`** during an immersive AR/MR session and let developers interact with its ordinary HTML/CSS/JavaScript UI using desktop mouse, keyboard, and native browser DOM events.

- **Generic Android Phone (ARCore):** Prefer the existing `src/polyfill/DOMOverlay.ts` approach that projects live DOM over the virtual phone screen. If an arbitrary root cannot be safely projected, use a clearly documented, workable 2D screen-preview fallback.
- **Meta Quest 3 MR:** Show the **single original live DOM root** as a usable 2D foreground panel over the desktop MR preview. **Do not** require a duplicated stereo DOM tree, depth-correct eye projection, or controller-ray interaction.
- Prefer compatibility with existing WebXR apps that pass `domOverlay: {root}` in `requestSession()`. When the preview option is enabled, allow an eligible supported session to request the emulator's limited `dom-overlay` preview; report the chosen preview type honestly (e.g. desktop `screen` projection) and document that this is **not a claim of native UA DOM Overlay conformance**. When opt-in is disabled or the target/root is unsupported, preserve proper optional omission, required rejection, and null `domOverlayState`.
- The main success criterion is **visibility + actual DOM interaction + existing page event listeners producing application behavior**, not physical Quest fidelity or a complete implementation of every normative W3C behavior.

## Context

- Use the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), Issue/PR templates and English collaboration conventions. Start from `dev`; target PRs to `dev`.
- Existing useful work: [DOM Overlay feasibility](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/dom-overlay-feasibility.md), [implementation notes](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/dom-overlay-implementation.md), `src/polyfill/DOMOverlay.ts`, `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts`, `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts`, `tests/dom-overlay-production.ts`, `tests/dom-overlay-negotiation.ts`, and `tests/dom-overlay-prototype.ts`. The Android internal rendering tests already verify original-root identity, native click/focus, geometry and DPI changes; **do not treat those as public support or as proof that the older full-spec security requirements were met**.
- Existing unsafe XR-derived synthetic input through arbitrary iframe/closed shadow content must **not** be re-enabled. The initial preview should rely on **native desktop DOM pointer/keyboard/click/input events**, not forged XR controller poses, privileged messaging or synthetic `beforexrselect` sequences. Use browser security boundaries; do not attempt to work around cross-origin restrictions.
- The W3C [DOM Overlays Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-dom-overlays-1/) remains a **reference for a future standards-compliant implementation**, not the full acceptance target of this issue. Native `:xr-overlay` matching, UA styles/top-layer isolation, world-space ray hits, cross-origin XR-input forwarding restrictions and exact headset stereo DOM composition are intentionally out of scope for the limited preview.
- Keep strict TypeScript, Manifest V3 packaged code/CSP, Three.js r186, existing device profiles/modes, browser extension messaging, and current WebXR API regressions. No remote code or additional powerful browser permissions.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add a visible, explicitly opt-in **Interactive DOM Overlay Preview** setting/control in the DevTools panel (or equivalent clear local configuration), disabled by default; explain its emulator-only limitations in the UI and README. Keep configuration behavior deterministic and test reload/persistence as appropriate.
- [ ] Detect the application-supplied `domOverlay.root` on eligible immersive AR sessions when preview is enabled. Render the **actual same root** (no `cloneNode`, HTML serialization or duplicate form state), preserving pre-existing event listeners, mutable element state, focus and ordinary DOM event propagation. Ensure session startup does not unexpectedly destroy or reparent the application's content.
- [ ] On Android AR, provide a visibly aligned interactive overlay over the virtual phone where practical, reusing/adapting the existing live DOM projection; verify phone movement, resizing, DPR and native button/input interactions. Provide and document a usable fallback for unsupported layout/root situations instead of silently failing.
- [ ] On Quest 3 MR, show one interactive **flat desktop preview overlay** over the MR preview, with readable UI and native mouse/keyboard controls. **No requirement** for distinct stereo eye textures, headset-accurate placement, controller-ray interaction or hand tracking of DOM controls.
- [ ] Support representative native UI behaviors: click handlers, checkbox state changes, text input, change/input events, focus and basic scrolling; demonstrate that application listeners execute normally in the original page. Do not claim arbitrary custom elements, closed shadows, cross-origin iframe control or full CSS semantics work unless tested.
- [ ] Implement a clear opt-in negotiation policy for optional and required `dom-overlay` requests that is limited to preview-supported modes/roots; verify `session.enabledFeatures`, `session.domOverlayState` and rejection/omission behavior. The app-facing behavior may intentionally differ from native DOM Overlay; **document exactly where** rather than labeling it standards-conformant.
- [ ] Avoid synthetic XR-derived DOM input, controller-pose delivery to overlay descendants, cross-origin iframe targeting and privileged extension bridges. Use ordinary browser-native DOM interactions and do not bypass iframe/sandbox/shadow restrictions. If the chosen rendering mechanism needs extra isolation, gate or decline that case safely and document it. Regression-test ordinary page behavior and non-overlay input paths.
- [ ] Cleanly show/hide/restore the overlay across `XRSession.end()`, Quest mode/profile switching, page navigation/reload, root removal, view changes and extension reload. Restore modified styles/attributes and original DOM ownership where safe; detach observers/listeners and avoid stale interactive overlays.
- [ ] Add end-to-end Chrome/Chromium regression tests for both profiles' **visible original DOM**, native actions and app events, opt-in off/on, optional/required feature negotiation, viewport changes, session teardown and existing non-overlay VR/AR behavior. Screenshot/geometry checks should verify that the panel is actually visible, not just that a DOM node exists. Test a simple sample application without modifying its DOM Overlay API calls where possible.
- [ ] Run and accurately record `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, and applicable existing `npm run test:wpt`/`npm run test:samples`. Explicitly separate limited preview testing from full DOM Overlay conformance and identify unperformed Firefox runtime checks.
- [ ] Update README and `docs/webxr-conformance.md` with an easy preview-mode usage example, profile-specific behavior and limitations, and the **new limited product scope**. Preserve documentation of unfinished standards compliance for future work; do not declare the original full-spec Issues satisfied retroactively.
- [ ] Submit focused PR(s) against `dev`, use the PR template, and review according to repo guidelines. Close **this limited-preview Issue** only when its practical display/interaction criteria are met and validated; later full-standards enhancement can be handled by a separate Issue.

## Optional validation

- Check the Firefox MV3 package in a supported Firefox runtime if available.
- Exercise DOM Overlay pages from WebXR Samples, including forms/menus/scrolling, plus representative A-Frame or Three.js applications.
- Evaluate `three-html-render` (https://github.com/repalash/three-html-render) as a future integration option, but **do not make it or experimental HTML-in-Canvas support a prerequisite** for a usable 2D interactive preview.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Required feature demonstration, tests and documentation are pre-merge checks. Browser-store release and physical headset certification are out of scope.
